families.algorithmDescription: Calculates an invoice total from a subtotal, discount percentage, and sales tax percentage. The discount amount is stored in PIC 9(5)V99 without ROUNDED (truncating fractional cents toward zero), subtracted from the subtotal to yield the net amount, and taxed using COMPUTE TAX-AMT ROUNDED (half-up to 2 decimal places) before adding net and tax.

inputFields.name: SUBTOTAL
inputFields.description: Invoice subtotal before discount and tax

inputFields.name: TAX-PCT
inputFields.description: Sales tax percentage applied to net amount (e.g., 8.25 means 8.25%)

Each line has at most 20 characters. Decimal fields use exactly the fractionalDigits given in lexicalInputRules; integer fields have no decimal point.
contract.validInputDomain: SUBTOTAL in [0.00, 99999.99] with at most 2 decimal places; DISC-PCT in [0.00, 99.99] with at most 2 decimal places; TAX-PCT in [0.00, 99.99] with at most 2 decimal places.
contract.outputMeaning: Single scalar decimal representing FINAL-TOTAL at scale 2.
contract.outputNormalization: Trim surrounding whitespace, strip optional leading '+' sign and leading integer zeros (preserving '0' before the decimal point), and format as an exact decimal string with 2 fractional digits (0.00).
semanticAssumptions: Working-storage intermediate fields: DISC-AMT PIC 9(5)V99, NET-AMT PIC 9(5)V99, TAX-AMT PIC 9(5)V99, FINAL-TOTAL PIC 9(6)V99.
GnuCOBOL 3.2 COMPUTE without ROUNDED into DISC-AMT PIC 9(5)V99 truncates digits beyond 2 decimal places toward zero.
GnuCOBOL 3.2 default ROUNDED mode on TAX-AMT PIC 9(5)V99 rounds half-way values away from zero (equivalent to RoundingMode.HALF_UP for non-negative values).
contract.upstreamStdinFormat: Three newline-separated decimal strings representing SUBTOTAL, DISC-PCT, and TAX-PCT.

families.algorithmDescription: Computes a pro-rata subscription charge from an annual fee, days used, and a promotional credit. The annual fee is divided by 365 into an intermediate 4-decimal field (PIC 9(3)V9(4)) with ROUNDED, multiplied by days used into a 2-decimal gross charge field (PIC 9(5)V99) with ROUNDED (which truncates any sixth integer digit modulo 100000.00 when the rounded product reaches 100000.00), and reduced by the credit amount with a floor at 0.00.

inputFields.name: ANNUAL-FEE
inputFields.description: Annual subscription fee in dollars and cents

inputFields.name: DAYS-USED
inputFields.description: Number of billable days in the 365-day year

inputFields.name: CREDIT-AMT
inputFields.description: Promotional credit subtracted from gross charge, floored at zero

contract.stdinFormat: One canonical ASCII numeric field per line in inputFields order, no leading integer zeroes except zero itself, no plus sign, padding, separators or exponent notation. Each line has at most 20 characters. Decimal fields use exactly the fractionalDigits given in lexicalInputRules; integer fields have no decimal point.
contract.validInputDomain: ANNUAL-FEE in [0.00, 99999.99] with at most 2 decimal places; DAYS-USED integer in [0, 365]; CREDIT-AMT in [0.00, 9999.99] with at most 2 decimal places.
contract.outputMeaning: Single scalar decimal representing FINAL-CHG at scale 2.
contract.outputNormalization: Trim surrounding whitespace, strip optional leading '+' sign and leading integer zeros (preserving '0' before the decimal point), and format as an exact decimal string with 2 fractional digits (0.00).
semanticAssumptions: Working-storage intermediate fields: DAILY-RATE PIC 9(3)V9(4), GROSS-CHG PIC 9(5)V99, FINAL-CHG PIC 9(5)V99.
DAILY-RATE has explicit storage scale 4 (PIC 9(3)V9(4)) and is rounded half-up via ROUNDED before being multiplied by DAYS-USED.
GROSS-CHG has explicit storage PIC 9(5)V99 and is rounded half-up via ROUNDED to scale 2, then truncated to 5 integer digits (modulo 100000.00) before comparing against CREDIT-AMT.
contract.upstreamStdinFormat: Three newline-separated strings: ANNUAL-FEE (decimal), DAYS-USED (integer), and CREDIT-AMT (decimal).

families.algorithmDescription: Performs a triangulated foreign-exchange conversion from a base currency amount using two sequential 4-decimal rates and a fixed settlement wire fee. The intermediate amount MID-AMT is stored in PIC 9(6)V9(4) without ROUNDED (truncating fractional digits beyond scale 4 toward zero), multiplied by the second rate into SETTLE-AMT PIC 9(6)V99 with ROUNDED (half-up to scale 2), and reduced by WIRE-FEE.

inputFields.name: RATE-A
inputFields.description: First leg conversion rate to intermediate currency

inputFields.name: RATE-B
inputFields.description: Second leg conversion rate from intermediate to settlement currency

inputFields.name: WIRE-FEE
inputFields.description: Fixed wire fee deducted in settlement currency

contract.stdinFormat: One canonical ASCII numeric field per line in inputFields order, no leading integer zeroes except zero itself, no plus sign, padding, separators or exponent notation. Each line has at most 20 characters. Decimal fields use exactly the fractionalDigits given in lexicalInputRules; integer fields have no decimal point.
contract.validInputDomain: BASE-AMT in [100.00, 1000.00] with at most 2 decimal places; RATE-A in [0.5000, 10.0000] with at most 4 decimal places; RATE-B in [0.5000, 80.0000] with at most 4 decimal places; WIRE-FEE in [0.00, 25.00] with at most 2 decimal places.
contract.outputMeaning: Single scalar decimal representing NET-OUT in settlement currency at scale 2.
contract.outputNormalization: Trim surrounding whitespace, strip optional leading '+' sign and leading integer zeros (preserving '0' before the decimal point), and format as an exact decimal string with 2 fractional digits (0.00).
semanticAssumptions: Working-storage intermediate fields: MID-AMT PIC 9(6)V9(4), SETTLE-AMT PIC 9(6)V99, NET-OUT PIC 9(6)V99.

Across the declared valid input domain, MID-AMT lies in [50.0000, 10000.0000] and SETTLE-AMT lies in [25.00, 800000.00], so neither overflows its integer width and SETTLE-AMT is always greater than or equal to WIRE-FEE.
COMPUTE MID-AMT without ROUNDED truncates digits beyond 4 decimal places toward zero; COMPUTE SETTLE-AMT ROUNDED rounds half-way values away from zero at 2 decimal places.
contract.upstreamStdinFormat: Four newline-separated decimal strings representing BASE-AMT, RATE-A, RATE-B, and WIRE-FEE.

families.algorithmDescription: Computes the weighted average unit inventory cost across two purchase lots. Each lot's quantity (PIC 9(3)) and unit cost (PIC 9(3)V99) are multiplied into exact 2-decimal extended cost fields (EXT-1 and EXT-2, PIC 9(6)V99), the quantities are summed into TOT-QTY (PIC 9(4)), and the combined extended cost is divided by TOT-QTY into UNIT-AVG (PIC 9(4)V99) using ROUNDED (half-up to 2 decimal places).

contract.stdinFormat: One canonical ASCII numeric field per line in inputFields order, no leading integer zeroes except zero itself, no plus sign, padding, separators or exponent notation. Each line has at most 20 characters. Decimal fields use exactly the fractionalDigits given in lexicalInputRules; integer fields have no decimal point.
contract.validInputDomain: QTY-1 and QTY-2 integers in [1, 999]; COST-1 and COST-2 decimals in [0.00, 999.99] with at most 2 decimal places.
contract.outputMeaning: Single scalar decimal representing the weighted average unit cost UNIT-AVG at scale 2.
contract.outputNormalization: Trim surrounding whitespace, strip optional leading '+' sign and leading integer zeros (preserving '0' before the decimal point), and format as an exact decimal string with 2 fractional digits (0.00).
semanticAssumptions: Working-storage intermediate fields: EXT-1 PIC 9(6)V99, EXT-2 PIC 9(6)V99, TOT-QTY PIC 9(4), UNIT-AVG PIC 9(4)V99.

Because QTY-1 and QTY-2 are integers in [1, 999], TOT-QTY is in [2, 1998] (never zero), EXT-1 and EXT-2 are exact at scale 2 without truncation and bounded by 998990.01, and UNIT-AVG is bounded by 999.99.
COMPUTE UNIT-AVG ROUNDED = (EXT-1 + EXT-2) / TOT-QTY divides total extended cost by total units and rounds half-way values away from zero at scale 2.
contract.upstreamStdinFormat: Four newline-separated strings: QTY-1 (integer), COST-1 (decimal), QTY-2 (integer), and COST-2 (decimal).
contract.lexicalScopeRevision: EXPLICIT_CANONICAL_SUBSET_R1: lexical representation is restricted; numeric value bounds remain unchanged. Earlier broad lexical claims are not inherited.

variants.labelRationale: Computes exact extended lot costs in J1, total quantity in J2, and divides total cost by totQty using RoundingMode.HALF_UP at scale 2 in J3 to match COMPUTE UNIT-AVG ROUNDED in C3.

variants.labelRationale: Segment J3 aligns with C3 as the unit-average computation step but computes the unweighted mean (cost1 + cost2) / 2 instead of the quantity-weighted mean (ext1 + ext2) / totQty. families.algorithmDescription: Multiply one nonnegative amount by one four-decimal FX rate, round to cents half-up, then round to the nearest 0.05 cash denomination and output one scale-two amount.
families.structuralIndependenceRationale: Actual source contains one multiply, a scale-two rounding boundary, rounded denomination division, and reconstruction. F001 has two dependent percentages around a net amount; F003 has two FX multiplications, a scale-four truncation boundary, and a fee. Independent initialization is reordered in Java; the algorithmic steps remain dependent. This rationale does not certify cross-corpus independence.

inputFields.name: EXCHANGE-RATE
inputFields.description: Nonnegative local units per foreign unit.

contract.stdinFormat: Two newline-separated canonical ASCII decimals: amount with exactly 2 fractional digits, then rate with exactly 4. No leading integer zeroes except the single zero before the decimal point, signs, spaces, separators, or exponent notation. Each line is at most 20 characters.
contract.validInputDomain: Amount in [0.00,50000.00]; rate in [0.0000,9.9999]. Programs assume these valid inputs; invalid-input behavior is outside the contract.
contract.outputMeaning: One nonnegative scalar local-currency amount at scale two, a multiple of 0.05.
contract.outputNormalization: Trim surrounding ASCII whitespace; remove an optional leading plus sign and leading integer zeroes while preserving one zero before the decimal point; require exactly two fractional digits. Thus COBOL 000120.00 and Java 120.00 normalize to 120.00.
semanticAssumptions: CASH-STEP PIC 9V99 is initialized to exactly 0.05.
RAW-LOCAL PIC 9(6)V9(6) stores the exact product of the two-place amount and four-place rate; no fractional product digit is discarded.
CENT-LOCAL PIC 9(6)V99 receives RAW-LOCAL with ROUNDED: nearest cent with half-way values away from zero, equivalent to HALF_UP on this nonnegative domain.

CASH-UNITS PIC 9(8) receives CENT-LOCAL/CASH-STEP with ROUNDED, using the same positive half-up rule. A half-denomination tie cannot occur after cent rounding: cent remainders 0,1,2 round down; 3,4 round up to the next multiple of five cents.
FINAL-LOCAL PIC 9(6)V99 is CASH-UNITS*CASH-STEP exactly; OUT-VAL PIC 9(6).99 supplies two output decimal places.
No original F005 runtime result applies to this revision.

staticBounds.conclusion: Every COBOL receiving field fits; Java long intermediates fit even for defective V4, and BigDecimal has no fixed precision MathContext. Division by 0.05 is terminating. These are static bounds, not compiler or runtime results.

families.alignmentScope: One-based inclusive lines. Segments cover cash-step initialization and all arithmetic. Declarations, input conversion, output editing, and boilerplate are intentionally outside the alignment scope. Every declared segment participates in an alignment.

variants.labelRationale: BigDecimal preserves exact six-place conversion, HALF_UP cent rounding, exact division by 0.05, integer HALF_UP unit rounding, and reconstruction. C4 maps to J4/J5. Cash-step initialization moves after the independent raw conversion.

executionEvidence.scope: Finite offline curation replay only, not proof or unseen model evaluation.

families.algorithmDescription: Updates an account balance by adding a signed adjustment (ADJ-AMT, PIC S9(5)) to an opening balance (START-BAL, PIC 9(5)) into an unsigned intermediate balance field (MID-BAL, PIC 9(5)), which strips the negative sign (coercing negative intermediate sums to their positive absolute magnitude), and then subtracts a signed fee (FEE-AMT, PIC S9(4)) into a signed final balance (END-BAL, PIC S9(6)).

inputFields.name: ADJ-AMT
inputFields.description: Signed integer adjustment added to opening balance

inputFields.name: FEE-AMT
inputFields.description: Signed integer fee subtracted from intermediate balance

contract.stdinFormat: Three newline-separated canonical ASCII integer strings (at most 20 characters per line, optional leading '-' on ADJ-AMT and FEE-AMT only, no '+' sign, no exponent notation, no padding or separators) representing START-BAL, ADJ-AMT, and FEE-AMT.
contract.validInputDomain: START-BAL canonical ASCII integer in [0, 40000]; ADJ-AMT canonical ASCII integer in [-40000, 40000]; FEE-AMT canonical ASCII integer in [-5000, 5000]; each line length in [1, 20].
contract.outputMeaning: Single signed scalar integer representing END-BAL.
contract.outputNormalization: Trim surrounding whitespace, preserve a leading '-' sign for negative values, strip optional leading '+' sign and leading zeros from the digit sequence (preserving '0' for zero), and format as an exact integer string.
semanticAssumptions: Working-storage intermediate fields: MID-BAL PIC 9(5) (unsigned), END-BAL PIC S9(6) (signed).

Across the declared valid input domain, |START-BAL + ADJ-AMT| <= 80000, so storing into MID-BAL PIC 9(5) never overflows 5 digits, but because MID-BAL lacks an 'S' sign designation, GnuCOBOL 3.2 stores the absolute value |START-BAL + ADJ-AMT|.
END-BAL has PIC S9(6) and retains a negative sign when MID-BAL - FEE-AMT is negative.

variants.labelRationale: Uses 32-bit integer arithmetic with reordered and one-to-many segment mappings: C2 is split across J1 (pre-negating feeAmt) and J4 (adding feeDelta to midBal), while C1 is split across J2 (signed sum) and J3 (unsigned PIC 9(5) sign removal).
